title: save/fight.js serialises live SoulsAI as plain object; boot-check blind to it
next_step: extend boot-check to step after a load; consumption + delete-the-fix; blog line; name the damaged probes
notes: combat/ai.js and combat/enemy.js are declared by W1-12 [done] and W1-03 [fixed]; neither is building and both files were clean in the working tree when claimed. Declared here rather than left to read as a collision (rule 16).
NOT touching game/src/engine.js: 8 live pieces, working tree MM (staged AND unstaged neighbour edits). A `git commit --only game/src/engine.js` would carry them.

PRE-FIX REPRODUCTION (commit 63f41ef + working tree, one browser): ctl.ai constructor SoulsAI -> Object across saveRoundTrip(); ai.step is not a function on the next stepFrames(1); hash_equal false; the serialised SoulsAI is 81,892 of the 194,161-byte save (42%) because it drags the whole CombatBody, statblock and ai.json along with it.

SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND, NOT MINE TO FIX: game/src/engine.js:7182 nulls this.death.lastGrounded on every load where the death surface is not active, one statement after DeathSystem.restoreInFlight() restored it -- so death.last_grounded is the OTHER half of hash_equal:false and the D3 fall-rule respawn point does not survive a load. Same family as the comment four lines above it. Handed up.

FLEET NOTE: at the start of this run the whole tree was unbootable (Engine._installCanon threw on 2 unresolved canon refs after bank 63f41ef swept W1-17's in-flight removal of the `notary` infos). Someone demoted the throw to a warning mid-run and boot-check went green again. Not my change.

fix.what: save/fight.js now classifies every actor field: a LIVE OBJECT (class instance) is carried through its own saveState()/loadState() -- the contract Rig already had in combat/skeleton.js -- or it is not carried at all and is named in __unsaved. loadActor never assigns a plain object over a live one. SoulsAI grew saveState/loadState with an explicit MACHINERY set (b, stat, cfg, A, omega, sightR, walk, sprint, leashHard -- all pure functions of the statblock and ai.json, all rebuilt by the constructor) and an AI_FRAME_STAMPS set so its nine clocks are rebased like the body's. EnemyController._resolveAI() re-resolves when behaviour is 'souls' but ai is null, which is the load path.
fix.why_not_SKIP: EnemyController._idleBehaviour() guards its whole souls branch with `if (this.ai)`, so adding `ai` to SKIP would have restored it as null and the enemy would stop thinking without throwing -- the quieter, worse half of the same defect. Same shape as `post` in save/state.js.

measured_after.hash_equal_residual: death.last_grounded ONLY -- engine.js:7182, not this piece's file
